title: Restriction of the derived coefficient mate equals the projection morphism
statement:
Let $f:Z\to W$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $L_T=-\otimes_A^LB:D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ for ordinary derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $U_T$ for exact restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], for $T=Z,W$. Write $f_A^{-1}\dashv Rf_{*,A}$ and $f_B^{-1}\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ for the canonical adjunctions of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and $\varepsilon_{f,A}$ for the first counit. Use the canonical tensor/pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to identify $f_B^{-1}L_W$ with $L_Zf_A^{-1}$.

Let $J\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and assume $L_ZJ\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and $M=L_W(Rf_{*,A}J)\in D^+(W_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. Define the $B$-linear map $\beta_J:M\to Rf_{*,B}L_ZJ$ to be the adjoint transpose under $f_B^{-1}\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ of
$$f_B^{-1}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Z(f_A^{-1}Rf_{*,A}J)\xrightarrow{L_Z(\varepsilon_{f,A,J})}L_ZJ.$$
Under the canonical identifications $U_TL_TC\cong C\otimes_A^LB_T$ and $U_WRf_{*,B}N\cong Rf_{*,A}U_ZN$, the latter for bounded-below $N$ [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons], the morphism $U_W(\beta_J)$ is exactly
$$\mathrm{PF}_f(J,B_W[0]):(Rf_{*,A}J)\otimes_A^LB_W\longrightarrow Rf_{*,A}(J\otimes_A^LB_Z),$$
the canonical projection-formula morphism of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], where $f_A^{-1}B_W=B_Z$. This is an equality of the specified morphisms, natural in $J$ on the stated bounded-below domain; it asserts no properness, torsion, flatness or invertibility hypothesis and no isomorphism conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0GL6, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings: the identification of scalar change with the projection formula, before the proper/open composition.
